channel.title: Notes — Platform & reliability
channel.description: Platform, delivery, reliability, and DevSecOps notes.

item.title: Instrument Java, Python, and LLM calls without changing application code
item.description: A hands-on OrbStack walkthrough: Argo CD, the OpenTelemetry Operator, CloudNativePG, Grafana, Jaeger, k6, and an end-to-end trace.

item.title: Secure CI/CD is a path, not a scanner
item.description: Checks that stop real risk, then a signed release—so teams can trust what left the pipeline.

item.title: One golden path for trusted software
item.description: Deploy what secure CI/CD already signed—policy rejects the rest, so delivery stays boring and safe.

item.title: Progressive delivery can wait—make Git the only path to prod
item.description: Before canaries and flags, close the side doors. A single merge path beats a sophisticated rollout on a leaky pipeline.

item.title: Error budgets are a product conversation
item.description: Reliability only sticks when product owns the tradeoff—not when SRE alone owns the pager.

item.title: Golden paths without a portal of hope
item.description: A thin portal over excellent defaults beats a beautiful catalog of unfinished roads.

item.title: Admission policies that teams actually keep
item.description: Policy-as-code only works when engineers can read the intent and fix violations without a ticket lottery.

item.title: Right-sizing clusters before the invoice arrives
item.description: FinOps without SLOs is just cutting. Start with request hygiene, then let the autoscaler reclaim idle capacity.

item.title: What “on-call ready” means for a new platform
item.description: A platform is not ready when the demo works—it is ready when the first 3am page has a path to diagnosis.
